title: Coastal Erosion
objective: After this level you can explain how coasts wear away and how people defend them.
summary: Storms and waves move beach sand, and coasts starved of sediment retreat. Groins and seawalls can shift the loss elsewhere, softer fixes help, and sometimes people move instead.

cards.headline: In 1999, a brick lighthouse was moved about 880 m inland.
cards.body: When the Cape Hatteras Lighthouse was finished in 1870, it stood about 460 m from the ocean. By 1970, erosion had left it about 37 m from the water's edge. The lighthouse hadn't moved. The coast had.

cards.headline: Where the beach goes
cards.body: A beach is sand on the move. Breaking waves carry it along the coast, taking it from one stretch and dropping it on another, and storms are the main cause of beach erosion along many coasts. A beach also needs fresh supplies. Remember Level 61's rivers delivering sand? Coasts starved of sediment erode and migrate inland.

cards.headline: Three ways to hold a coast

items.label: Groins
points: Walls built out across the beach
Trap sand on the updrift side

items.label: Seawalls
points: The beach in front can disappear
Then waves hit the wall head-on

items.label: Softer fixes
points: Adding sand: costly and not permanent
Living shorelines: plants, sand, rock or oyster shells

cards.headline: Rising water, moving coasts
cards.body: The sea is also rising. A February 2022 report by NOAA, NASA and other US agencies projected that sea level along US coasts will rise 25 to 30 cm on average by 2050, about as much as in the previous 100 years. USGS studies project that beaches and coastal cliffs will erode faster as it does. Hatteras shows the last option: after groins and new sand, the lighthouse itself moved.

cards.headline: Erosion: faced
learned: Storms and waves move beach sand
Coasts starved of sediment retreat inland
Groins and seawalls shift the loss elsewhere
US seas: 25 to 30 cm higher by 2050 (2022 report)

questions.prompt: According to the USGS, what is the main cause of beach erosion along many coasts?

options.label: Tides rising and falling each day
options.rationale: Tides move water daily, but storms do the most damage.

options.label: Rivers bringing in new sand
options.rationale: River sand feeds beaches rather than eroding them.

options.label: Wind blowing the dunes inland
options.rationale: Storms are the primary cause named.

questions.explanation: Storms are the primary cause of beach erosion along many coasts; breaking waves also move sand along the shore.

questions.prompt: A town builds a groin to save its beach. Why might the beach just down the coast shrink?

options.label: It traps sand that would have drifted on
It makes the waves taller all along the coast
options.rationale: The problem is the sand supply, not wave height.

options.label: It pulls the sand out into deeper water
options.rationale: It holds sand on its own updrift side.

options.label: It blocks rivers from reaching the coast
options.rationale: Groins stop sand moving along the beach.

questions.explanation: A groin traps sand on its updrift side, so the beach downdrift loses sand to the continuing longshore movement.

questions.prompt: From Level 38, the sea's rise is speeding up. What do USGS studies project for beaches and coastal cliffs as it rises?

options.label: They will stay put behind the waterline
options.rationale: A rising sea eats into the coast.

options.label: They will grow as new sand washes in
options.rationale: The projection is for faster erosion.

options.label: They will rise along with the sea
options.rationale: Coasts don't lift themselves; they erode.

questions.explanation: USGS studies project that beaches and coastal cliffs will erode faster as sea level rises.
